title: 9 Best Soaps for Itching and Rashes Dermatologist-Recommended
summary: Stop the scratch! Find the best medicated and moisturizing soaps to soothe itchy skin, heal rashes, and restore your skin barrier according to your skin type.
body_text: Why Does Your Skin Feel Itchy? How to Choose the Best Soap? 9 Best Soaps for Dry Skin Best Itching Soap for Different Skin Types Ingredients to Avoid Using Tips for Soap FAQs If you've ever scratched your arms or legs throughout the day you're not alone. Rashes, fungal infections, and persistent itching can make your full day uncomfortable and irritated. You should avoid some rough fabrics because they can cause rashes or irritation. The itching may even keep you awake at night. These skin concerns affect sleep cycle, confidence, and daily comfort. Using the wrong soap for itching and rash can worsen irritation without you even realizing it. Many people are unaware that the antifungal soap in the shower may be worsening their skin issues, causing flares or interacting with an existing skin disease such as eczema or an allergy. We'll go through this article why skin becomes itchy or prone to rashes, how to select the right skin soap for itchiness. What ingredients really help to soothe skin irritation, and how to use soap correctly to see a real difference instead of a quick fix. If you're searching for the best soap for itchy skin, the best medicated soap for rashes, or just a kinder, less irritating body soap for itchy skin that will not irritate sensitive areas this guide will help you make an informed choice. Why Does Your Skin Feel Itchy or Develop Rashes? Itchy skin and rashes can occur due to allergies, dryness, eczema, fungal infections, harsh skincare products, or environmental factors. Understanding the reasons that cause helps you choose the most suitable soap for dry itchy skin: Dry skin (xerosis): Take hot showers, low humidity and use harsh and strong fragrance soaps strips natural oil and leave the skin dry and itchy. Dermatitis and Eczema: Chronic inflammatory conditions that cause red, itchy, sometimes weeping patches often worsened by fragranced or sulfate-based soaps. Allergic reactions: Get in touch with rough fabric, detergents or some artificial soap ingredients can cause redness, rashes and itchiness. Heat and sweat: Excess sweating especially in humid climates, can cause prickly heat and body itching, particularly in skin folds. Fungal or bacterial imbalances: An overgrowth of skin flora can cause itching along with visible rashes or bumps. Harsh cleansing habits: Over-scrubbing on body and soaps with a high pH or strong detergents (like SLS) disrupt the skin's natural oil. How to Choose the Best Soap for Itching and Rashes? Not every "gentle" or "moisturizing" soap on the shelf is actually suited for itchy or rash-prone skin. Here's what to actually check before buying: Check the pH: Healthy skin sits around pH 4.5–5.5. Regular bar soaps are often highly alkaline pH level approx H 9-10 which disrupts the natural skin barrier. Always look for pH-balanced or syndet (synthetic detergent) bars. Avoid known irritants: Skip soaps loaded with artificial fragrance, dyes, sulfates, and alcohol these are common triggers for itching and rashes. Look for barrier-supporting ingredients: Ceramides, colloidal oatmeal, glycerin, and shea butter help repair and maintain the skin barrier instead of just cleaning it away. Match it to your specific concern: A soap for eczema-prone skin isn't the same as one for oily, acne-prone skin with occasional rashes. Texture and active ingredients should differ. Consider medicated options when needed: If your itching is linked to a diagnosed condition (fungal infection, dandruff-related body itching, severe eczema), a dermatologist-recommended medicated soap for itchy skin with ingredients like zinc pyrithione may be more appropriate than a purely cosmetic one. Patch test first: Even "hypoallergenic" labeled products can react differently on different skin types, so a small patch test on the inner arm for 24–48 hours is a smart first step. Prefer soap-free or low-lather formulas: Excessive lather usually means more surfactants, which can mean more stripping of natural oils. 9 Best Soaps for Dry and Itchy Skin Here are the top soaps based on ingredients, skin type, and key benefits to quickly find the best option for your skin concern. Product Name Main Ingredients Primary Benefits Mesoketz Medicated Soap Ketoconazole (2% w/w) Fights against skin infections caused by fungi and reduces itching and flaking. Triketo-AF Soap Ketoconazole (2%), Cetrimide (0.5%) Destroys fungal infection and reduces the number of microbes on skin. DewSka Moisturising Soap Shea Butter, Olive Extract, Almond Oil Helps in deep hydration, nourishment, and healing of scaly winter skin. Dewmoist Soap Aloe Vera, Shea Blend, Olive Oil, Jojoba Oil Gently cleanses without disturbing the natural skin moisture. Kz Plus Medicated Soap Ketoconazole (2% w/w) Dermatologist-recommended bar that eliminates infection-causing fungi. Konaz 2% Soap Ketoconazole (2%), Kokum Butter, Glycerin Anti-fungal skin infection treatment with deep moisturization. KetoSka Antifungal Soap Ketoconazole (2%), Glycerine, Olive Oil Destroys fungi causing infection and itching and redness. Swisscosmed Lulichem Soap Luliconazole (1% w/w) Disrupts fungal cell membranes to effectively eliminate topical infections. Leirfaith Scalefree Soap Ketoconazole (2% w/w) Eliminates the infection-causing fungus and prevents its spread. 1. Mesoketz Medicated Soap Mesoketz Medicated Soap is formulated with Ketoconazole to target fungal skin infections at the source. It's a go-to option when itching and rashes are linked to an active fungal condition rather than simple dryness. Why buy: Targets fungal infections like ringworm, athlete's foot, and candida-related skin infections at the source, helping calm the itching, redness, and flaking they cause. Best for: Itching and rashes linked to a diagnosed fungal skin or scalp infection, used under medical guidance. 2. Triketo-AF Soap Triketo-AF Soap is a bodywash that combines antifungal and antibacterial action with ingredients aimed at reducing the urge to scratch. It's suited to itching that has more than one underlying cause. Why buy: Combines antifungal, antibacterial, and anti-pruritic (anti-itch) action in one wash, addressing both the infection and the itch sensation. Best for: Body itching with a suspected fungal or bacterial component, especially in sweat-prone areas. 3. DewSka Moisturising Soap DewSka Moisturising Soap is a cosmetic, non-medicated bar built around hydrating, skin-loving ingredients. It's designed for everyday use rather than treating an active infection. Why buy: A cosmetic (non-medicated) moisturizing bar that hydrates while cleansing, without stripping the skin. Best for: Dry, rough, or flaky skin causing itching, and everyday use for sensitive or normal skin. 4. Dewmoist Soap Dewmoist Soap is a gentle cleansing bar aimed at restoring the skin's natural moisture balance. It leans on emollient-rich ingredients rather than active medication. Why buy: Gentle, soap-free formula that hydrates while cleansing, helping restore the skin's moisture balance without irritation. Best for: Dry, sensitive, or irritated skin that needs daily gentle care rather than active medication. 5. Kz Plus Medicated Soap Kz Plus Medicated Soap is an antifungal bar aimed at clearing common fungal skin infections while easing the itching and irritation they cause. It's typically used as part of a prescribed treatment course. Why buy: Clears fungal infections such as ringworm, jock itch, and athlete's foot while directly relieving the itching, redness, and scaling they cause. Best for: Diagnosed fungal skin infections and fungal-related dandruff, used as prescribed by a doctor. 6. Konaz 2% Soap Konaz 2% Soap pairs an antifungal active with moisturizing ingredients, so it treats the infection without leaving skin feeling stripped. It's a balanced option for infection-prone, itchy skin. Why buy: Also contains glycerin and kokum butter, so it treats the fungal infection while helping keep skin from feeling stripped or dry. Best for: Itchy, irritated, or infection-prone skin needing antifungal treatment alongside some moisturization. 7. KetoSka Antifungal Soap KetoSka Antifungal Soap targets fungal causes of common scalp and skin issues while including emollients to support the skin barrier. It's formulated for regular use on affected areas. Why buy: Targets fungal causes of dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and skin infections while nourishing the skin barrier with emollients. Best for: Fungal-related itching, flaking, and redness on body or scalp-adjacent skin. 8. Swisscosmed Lulichem Medicated Antifungal Soap Swisscosmed Lulichem Medicated Antifungal Soap uses a different antifungal active than most ketoconazole-based bars, making it an alternative when that's specifically prescribed. It's aimed at clearing infection rather than general dryness. Why buy: An alternative antifungal active for those who need or are prescribed luliconazole over ketoconazole for infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, or ringworm. Best for: Doctor-diagnosed fungal skin infections, particularly when advised as a luliconazole-based treatment. 9. Leirfaith Scalefree Soap Leirfaith Scalefree Soap is an antifungal bar designed to clear infection while reducing the irritation that comes with it. It's meant for consistent, prescribed use rather than occasional cleansing. Why buy: Treats fungal infections like ringworm, athlete's foot, and thrush while reducing the irritation, redness, and itching that come with them. Best for: Fungal skin infections needing consistent, prescribed antifungal cleansing. Best Soap for Itching and Rashes Based on Skin Type Different skin types require different formulations. Here's how to choose the right cleansing soap based on your skin's needs. For Dry, Itchy Skin Priority is intense hydration paired with gentle cleansing. The best soap for dry and itchy skin is typically a creamy, low-lather bar or syndet using glycerin, shea butter, or colloidal oatmeal as core ingredients rather than harsh detergents. These formulas cleanse without pulling moisture out of the skin — essential since dry skin already has a compromised barrier that struggles to retain hydration. Look for a soap for dry itchy skin labeled fragrance-free and pH-balanced. Avoid anything that leaves skin feeling tight or "squeaky-clean" right after rinsing — that squeaky feeling usually means natural oils have been stripped away. For Sensitive Skin Sensitive skin reacts quickly to fragrances, dyes, preservatives, and strong surfactants, so the goal is minimal ingredients and maximum gentleness. A good soap for sensitive itchy skin should be free of artificial fragrance and colorants, formulated at a skin-friendly pH, and ideally dermatologically tested. Aloe vera and glycerin-based cleansers work particularly well they soothe on contact while cleansing gently. Redness, stinging, or a rash shortly after using a new soap usually signals the formula is too harsh. Switching to a fragrance-free, minimal-ingredient bar is often the simplest fix. For Eczema-Prone Skin Eczema-prone skin needs a cleanser that actively supports the skin barrier, not just one that avoids irritants. Ceramide-enriched, soap-free cleansing bars are usually the top recommendation, since ceramides are naturally occurring lipids that eczema-prone skin often lacks. These formulas cleanse without disturbing the skin's already fragile barrier, helping reduce the frequency and intensity of flare-ups over time. Pair this kind of soap with a fragrance-free moisturizer immediately after bathing (while skin is still damp) for the best long-term itch relief. For Allergy-Prone Skin Skin that reacts to new products, fabrics, or environmental triggers with hives, redness, or itching benefits most from hypoallergenic, fragrance-free formulations with the shortest possible ingredient list. The best soap for skin allergies avoids common allergens like parabens, sulfates, synthetic dyes, and strong essential oils. Soothing ingredients like aloe vera or oat extract help calm reactive skin. The real key is consistency stick to one well-tolerated, simple formula rather than frequently switching products, since frequent changes make it harder to identify and avoid your specific triggers. For Oily Skin with Rashes Oily skin can still develop itching and rashes, often due to clogged pores, sweat buildup, or reactions to heavy, occlusive products. The goal is balance: a cleanser that controls excess oil and sweat without over-drying the skin, which can ironically trigger more irritation. Lightweight, sulfate-free gel washes with mild surfactants and calming ingredients like niacinamide work well, since they clean thoroughly without leaving a heavy residue. Avoid strong antibacterial bars that promise deep oil control these often over-strip the skin and can worsen itching over time. Ingredients That Help Relieve Itching and Skin Irritation Certain ingredients calm inflammation, restore the skin barrier, and lock in moisture to reduce itching and discomfort. Colloidal Oatmeal Colloidal oatmeal is one of the most well-known skin care ingredients for irritated and itchy skin. It creates a protective barrier on the skin and holds moisture. It contains natural anti-inflammatory properties and compounds known as avenanthramides that are particularly beneficial for skin that is itchy and red and also good for eczema and overall sensitive skin Glycerin Glycerin is a humectant which pulls moisture into the skin and helps retain it. It is used in almost all dermatologist recommended soaps to counteract the drying effect of the surfactants. Ceramides The ceramides are naturally occurring lipids within the skin barrier that act as the "mortar" that holds the skin cells together. In eczema and chronically dry skin ceramide levels are often depleted, and moisture is easily lost from the skin barrier. Soaps that contain ceramide can replenish this barrier and help to reduce both dryness and itching. Shea Butter Rich in fatty acids and vitamins, shea butter deeply moisturizes and forms a soothing layer over irritated skin. Most helpful for very dry, flaky or rough areas that itch more strongly in cool, low humidity weather. Aloe Vera Known for its natural cooling and anti-inflammatory effects. It can help alleviate mild irritation caused by sunburn, as well as itching and redness. It has light consistency and non-greasy formula that makes it great for sensitive skin or prone to allergies. Zinc Pyrithione The zinc pyrithione ingredient works against fungal infections and rashes. It is often added to medicated soaps for fungal related itching or dandruff. Almost used in medicated soap for itchy or rashes caused by fungi after being recommended by dermatologist. Ingredients to Avoid if You Have Itchy or Irritated Skin Some ingredients can worsen irritation and prolong skin discomfort. Avoid these if your skin is already inflamed or sensitive. Artificial Fragrances Synthetic fragrances are among the top allergens and possible irritants to contact dermatitis. Fragrance-free is almost always the better option even if the product is described as “lightly scented,” as these fragrances can trigger flares in sensitive and eczema-prone skin. Sulfates (SLS/SLES) Sodium Lauryl Sulfate and Sodium Laureth Sulfate are strong foaming agents which are very effective in cleaning. It also remove the natural oils and makes the skin barrier weaker. Sulfate-free formulas are highly recommended for anyone who suffers from dryness, itching or rashes. Alcohol-Based Cleansers Some alcohols especially denatured or isopropyl alcohol (which is used to make it feel "clean") are very drying and irritating, particularly on already damaged skin. These tend to make skin irritated and itchy even if they immediately feel refreshing. Harsh Exfoliating Particles Avoid scrubs and soaps containing coarse exfoliating beads or particles they can cause rashes and make people more susceptible to infection if their skin is already irritated or inflamed. If skin is itchy or rash, it should be avoided for physical exfoliation until it has fully healed. Strong Antibacterial Agents Avoid using soaps that are too harsh and will throw off the balance of the natural microbes present in the skin and remove protective oils. It leads to increased skin irritation and itching over the longer term, particularly when using these products every day. How to Use Soap Correctly for Itchy and Rash-Prone Skin Even the best soap won't work effectively if used incorrectly. Follow these dermatologist-recommended cleansing tips for healthier skin. Use lukewarm water, not hot: Hot water feels soothing in the moment but strips natural oils and worsens dryness and itching afterward. Keep showers short: Long showers, especially with soap covering large areas, increase moisture loss from the skin. Apply gently, don't scrub: Use your hands or a soft cloth rather than rough loofahs, especially on rashes or already irritated patches. Rinse thoroughly: Leftover soap residue can itself be irritating, so make sure all product is rinsed off completely. Pat dry, don't rub: Rubbing with a towel can aggravate itchy skin; gently patting dry is far less irritating. Moisturize immediately after: Apply a fragrance-free moisturizer within a few minutes of bathing, while skin is still slightly damp, to lock in hydration. Avoid over-washing: Washing too frequently, especially with strong soaps, can worsen dryness and itching over time once or twice daily is usually enough for most people. Introduce new soaps gradually: When switching to a new soap for itching and rashes, patch test first and monitor your skin for a few days before regular use. Final Thoughts on Soaps for Itchy Skin Itchy skin and rashes rarely have one single cause which is why the right soap looks different for everyone. Before picking a product, it helps to identify what's actually triggering your discomfort, whether it's dryness, sensitivity, eczema, allergies, or a fungal infection, since each needs a different approach. For everyday dryness or sensitivity, gentle, fragrance-free, pH-balanced soaps work best, while medicated antifungal soaps should be reserved for diagnosed infections and used under a doctor's guidance. Ingredients like colloidal oatmeal, glycerin, ceramides, shea butter, and aloe vera help support and repair the skin barrier. How you use the soap matters just as much as what's in it, so lukewarm water, short showers, and immediate moisturizing after bathing all go a long way. If itching or rashes persist despite the right routine, it's best to consult a dermatologist rather than continuing to self-treat.

title: Bench Accounting Alternatives in 2026: Where to Go Next
summary: Bench shut down. Here are the strongest alternatives in 2026 for startups and growing businesses, with a clear migration path, pricing, and fit guidance.
body_text: What happened to Bench, and why migration is urgent Bench Accounting, founded in 2012 and once self-described as North America’s largest bookkeeping service for small businesses, abruptly ceased operations on Friday, December 27, 2024, locking roughly 12,000 customers out of their books days before tax season. The shutdown carried no advance notice. Three days later, on December 30, 2024, Employer.com announced its acquisition of Bench out of insolvency , a deal stitched together by a company whose CEO had only acquired the employer.com domain weeks earlier for around $450,000. The financial picture behind the collapse was severe. On January 7, 2025, Bench Accounting and its subsidiary 10Sheet Services Inc. filed an assignment in bankruptcy in Canada. Filings revealed $2.8 million in cash against $65.4 million in liabilities, with $51 million owed to the National Bank of Canada, more than 85% of which was unsecured. On August 11, 2025, Employer.com officially rebranded Bench as part of Mainstreet , folding it together with two other recent acquisitions. The Bench-branded site now redirects most flows under Mainstreet’s umbrella. As of May 2026, Bench Accounting holds a D- rating from the Better Business Bureau and is not BBB-accredited, with recurring 2026 complaints citing late tax filings, missed-deadline penalties, unresponsive support, and forced tier upgrades. Why migration is urgent. Any business still on the platform is now relying on a brand that has been shut down once, sold once, and rebranded once, all inside nine months. Tax season 2026 filings, year-end 2025 closings, R&D credit claims, and audit prep all depend on a provider that may not be the same entity six months from now. Indinero has maintained continuous operations since 2009 with stable ownership and a 5-star Clutch rating, the kind of operational stability that matters most when your books underwrite every other decision your business makes. What Bench customers actually need in a replacement Bench’s value proposition was simple: hand off bookkeeping to a real human team and stop thinking about it. The replacement must match that simplicity while fixing the structural problems Bench customers are migrating away from. Data portability. Bench used a proprietary bookkeeping platform. Customers can’t export a clean QuickBooks Online or Xero file without manual rebuilding. Pilot publicly built a free Bench-to-QuickBooks migration service to capture stranded customers, which underscores how non-portable the data is. Any replacement should put your books inside a tool you own, QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, so a future provider change is a vendor swap, not a data-recovery project. GAAP-readiness. Bench was historically cash-basis-only. Growing companies above roughly $1M in revenue, and any company headed for an audit or institutional financing, need accrual-basis GAAP books. The migration is the right moment to convert. The IRS Publication 538 guidance on accounting methods is the technical reference. Catch-up bookkeeping. Many Bench customers experienced months of missed or delayed reconciliations across the shutdown and the post-acquisition transition. A replacement provider should price catch-up cleanly, not bury it inside an ambiguous onboarding fee. Tax filing continuity. Bench’s combined bookkeeping plus tax offering was its most cited feature. A replacement must either include tax filing or partner cleanly with a tax provider, especially mid-year when partial-year filings, extension management, and R&D credit windows are all live. Multi-state nexus exposure. Companies that grew on Bench may have crossed economic-nexus thresholds in additional states post- Wayfair without registering or filing. Any catch-up engagement needs a nexus exposure check baked in. For background, see Indinero’s sales tax expertise . R&D credit capture. Under the post-2022 Inflation Reduction Act rules, qualified small businesses can now offset up to $500,000 per year in payroll taxes using the Section 41 R&D credit on Form 6765, doubled from the prior $250,000 cap. Companies that skipped the credit while on Bench may be able to claim retrospectively. Operational stability of the new provider. The whole point of migration is to land somewhere that will still exist in 24 months. Track record, ownership stability, and provider scale all matter more now than they did before December 2024. The six strongest Bench alternatives in 2026 The six alternatives below are the names that consistently appear in industry shortlists. They span the full pricing band Bench used to cover, sub-$500/mo solopreneur tier through $5,000+/mo CFO-included engagements. 1. Indinero Positioning: All-in-one finance department. Bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory bundled under one fixed monthly engagement. Pricing: Starts at $750/mo, month-to-month, with no annual prepay required. Track record: Continuous operations since 2009 with stable ownership. 5-star Clutch rating. 500+ regular customers. 100+ years combined team experience. SOC 2 compliant (2026). Best fit: Growing companies in the $1M to $20M+ revenue band that need GAAP-clean accrual books, tax filing, and strategic CFO advisory under one team. Industry breadth: SaaS, ecommerce, construction, healthcare practices, nonprofits, professional services. Not VC-only. Where it wins for ex-Bench customers: Direct migration into QuickBooks or Xero (no proprietary platform), full GAAP conversion handled inside the engagement, tax filing under the same roof, and a 17-year operational track record. See the head-to-head Indinero vs Bench for a side-by-side comparison. 2. Pilot Positioning: Hybrid people-plus-software bookkeeping anchored on founder empathy. The most visible “Bench alternative” voice in the market post-shutdown. Pricing (as of May 2026, per Pilot’s pricing page ): Bookkeeping Essentials $99/mo (under $100K monthly expenses), Bookkeeping Core from $499/mo, Tax $1,000 to $2,450+/yr, CFO tiers $1,875/mo to $5,625/mo (billed annually), R&D credit at 20% of captured credit. Track record: 3,000+ customers. Clients have raised over $1B in venture capital. Best fit: Early-stage VC-backed startups that want a clean web app, predictable pricing, and an annual-prepay model for the CFO tier. Where it strains for ex-Bench customers: CFO tiers require annual prepay for best pricing. The top CFO Custom tier caps at $5,625/mo, which underweights companies past $5M revenue with deeper CFO needs. 3. Kruze Consulting Positioning: Expert accounting for VC-funded Delaware C-Corps. Best-in-category on R&D tax credit depth, 409A cadence, and Delaware franchise tax authority content. Pricing (per Kruze’s published pricing page): Basic bookkeeping plus tax in the $650 to $850/mo range, Founder Timesaver $850 to $1,500/mo, Premium custom-quoted (industry ranges of $8,000 to $25,000+/mo), R&D tax credit at 15% of captured credit with a $1,000 minimum. Audience restriction: Kruze publicly limits its service to funded Delaware C-Corps that have raised at least $500,000 in venture capital. Bootstrapped, PE-backed, LLC, S-Corp, and non-Delaware companies are not the target. Best fit: Funded Delaware C-Corps that need deep R&D credit work, 409A cadence, and Delaware franchise tax accuracy. For a direct comparison, see Indinero vs Kruze . 4. Bookkeeper360 Positioning: Generalist SMB and lower-mid-market accounting in operation since 2012. Strong Xero and QuickBooks parity, mobile app, payroll services. Pricing (per bookkeeper360.com/pricing, May 2026): Cleanup/onboarding from $1,000 one-time, Bookkeeping Monthly from $399/mo, Bookkeeping Weekly from $549/mo, Tax roughly $1,000 to $1,500/yr for business returns, Advisory from $700/mo, Coaching from $1,500/mo, Fractional CFO from $2,000/mo. Track record: 200+ Google reviews at 4.8/5. Founded 2012. Best fit: Small businesses up to lower mid-market that want straightforward Xero or QuickBooks bookkeeping with a payroll and tax bolt-on, plus a paid CFO add-on layered in later. Where it strains for ex-Bench customers: CPA-led strategic work is a separate tier add-on rather than bundled. The default offering is bookkeeper-led, not CPA-led. 5. Zeni Positioning: AI-first bookkeeping platform with a human controller team behind it. Brands itself as “The #1 AI Bookkeeping Software.” Pricing (per zeni.ai/pricing): Bookkeeping Starter $549/mo, Bookkeeping Growth $1,200/mo, Enterprise custom, CFO services from $1,599/mo Lite (with setup fee) up to $4,990+/mo Enterprise. Track record: Reports $20B+ in transactions managed annually. Headcount and client count not publicly disclosed. AI Agents product remains partly waitlist-gated. Best fit: Tech-forward startups that prioritize an AI-augmented dashboard view over a traditional CPA relationship. Where it strains for ex-Bench customers: The AI-first framing changes the operating model, not just the tool. Customers migrating from Bench precisely because automated bookkeeping failed them may not want another platform-centric provider. 6. Burkland Positioning: Pure fractional CFO with integrated finance, tax, and HR for VC-backed startups. The strongest fractional-CFO brand in the category. Pricing: Not publicly published. Industry-reported retainer ranges of roughly $3,000 to $15,000/mo, with hourly engagements typically $190 to $500/hr. Track record: 800+ startup clients. Clients have raised nearly $20B in venture capital across pre-seed through Series C. 60+ VC partnerships. Best fit: VC-backed startups (especially Series A and later) that need a dedicated fractional CFO, are comfortable with custom-quoted pricing, and value depth in fundraising support and board reporting. Where it strains for ex-Bench customers: Bench’s pricing transparency was a core part of its appeal. Burkland is custom-quote only, and Bench’s customer base was overwhelmingly bookkeeping-first, not CFO-first. Key differences across the alternatives A few cleavage lines separate these six providers in ways that matter to a migrating Bench customer. Reading the differences carefully will collapse the shortlist by half before you even take a sales call. Bundled vs unbundled. Indinero is the only provider in the set that bundles bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and CFO advisory under a single fixed monthly engagement. Pilot, Kruze, Bookkeeper360, Zeni, and Burkland each price two or more of those service lines as separate tiers, separate quotes, or separate add-ons. For ex-Bench customers who valued the single-bill, single-team model, the bundle matters. Indinero is your all-in-one finance department, CFO advisory, GAAP-clean books, tax, and 409A all under one monthly engagement starting at $750/mo. Pricing transparency. Indinero, Pilot, Bookkeeper360, and Zeni publish their starting prices on their public sites. Kruze publishes ranges. Burkland does not publish pricing. Transparency-sensitive customers will narrow the shortlist on that axis alone. Annual prepay vs month-to-month. Pilot’s best pricing requires annual prepay. Indinero is explicitly month-to-month. Bench customers should weigh the cost of being locked into another annual contract right after their previous provider’s annual contract evaporated. GAAP posture. Indinero, Pilot, Kruze, and Burkland operate GAAP-first by default. Bookkeeper360 supports accrual but charges more for it. Zeni’s AI-first product is GAAP-capable but not its lead message. Bench was historically cash-basis. For any company on a path to audit, due diligence, or institutional debt, GAAP-first is the migration baseline. See the audit preparation overview for what audit-ready actually requires. Audience fit. Kruze and Burkland are gated to VC-backed startups (Kruze explicitly so). Indinero, Pilot, Bookkeeper360, and Zeni accept a broader range of entities. For LLCs, S-Corps, PE-backed operators, bootstrapped founders, multi-entity structures, and non-Delaware companies, that audience breadth is a hard filter. Industry breadth. Pilot, Kruze, Burkland, and Zeni are tech-heavy. Indinero and Bookkeeper360 publish work across construction, healthcare, nonprofit, ecommerce, professional services, and other non-tech verticals. The right answer depends entirely on what industry you’re in. Pricing structure compared Approximate entry pricing for the tier each provider would actually steer a $1M to $5M revenue ex-Bench customer toward, as of May 2026: Provider Bookkeeping entry tier CFO tier entry Tax handling Indinero From $750/mo (bundled with tax + CFO advisory in higher tiers) Included in bundled engagement Included Pilot Core from $499/mo Basic $1,875/mo (annual prepay) Separate, $1,000 to $2,450+/yr by entity Kruze Basic from $650/mo Embedded in Founder Timesaver and Premium tiers Embedded Bookkeeper360 Monthly from $399/mo. Weekly from $549/mo Advisory $700/mo. Fractional CFO $2,000/mo Separate, $1,000 to $1,500/yr business returns Zeni Starter $549/mo. Growth $1,200/mo Lite $1,599/mo (+ setup fee) Tax tiers from $2,499/yr Burkland Custom quote (CFO-led model) Reported retainers $3,000 to $15,000/mo Embedded in broader engagement For reference, Bench’s last published bookkeeping tiers (pre-shutdown) were Essential at $299/mo and Premium at $499/mo, with tax-included tiers in the $600 to $700/mo band. Most ex-Bench customers will land at a higher monthly number than they were paying. That premium buys data portability, GAAP discipline, real human CPA escalation paths, and a provider that’s not currently mid-rebrand. Indinero pricing starts at $750/mo with month-to-month engagements, no annual commitments, no surprise upcharges. That structure is the deliberate counterweight to the annual-prepay model Bench customers just got burned by. With Indinero, the full finance function, bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory, is one monthly engagement, not three vendor contracts. Ideal customers: who each alternative fits The match between an ex-Bench customer and a provider depends almost entirely on revenue stage, entity structure, and how much strategic finance the business actually needs. Read this section against your own profile rather than as a generic ranking. Solopreneur or pre-revenue, under $250K in annual revenue. The Bench Essentials demographic. Most-fit: Pilot Essentials at $99/mo for sub-$100K monthly expenses, Bookkeeper360 Monthly, or a local bookkeeper. CFO advisory is overkill at this stage. Small business, $250K to $1M annual revenue. Most-fit: Bookkeeper360 (Monthly $399/mo or Weekly $549/mo) for a clean Xero or QuickBooks build, Pilot Core for SaaS-flavored businesses, or Indinero’s entry tier at $750/mo for businesses on a growth curve that will cross $1M in the next 12 months. Growth-stage, $1M to $20M annual revenue. This is Indinero’s core band. Bench customers in this range need GAAP-clean books, tax filing, multi-state nexus monitoring, R&D credit capture, and CFO-level advisory as one engagement. Pilot can serve here but its CFO tier caps out at $5,625/mo. Kruze can serve only if you’re a VC-backed Delaware C-Corp. Burkland can serve as a CFO add-on layered over a separate bookkeeper. VC-backed Delaware C-Corp, Series A through Series C. Most-fit: Kruze for tax and R&D credit depth, Pilot for predictable tiered pricing, or Burkland for fractional CFO depth. Indinero serves this segment too, and adds the bundled offering without the audience restriction. Bootstrapped or PE-backed operator, non-Delaware entity, or LLC / S-Corp. Most-fit: Indinero or Bookkeeper360. Kruze and Burkland aren’t designed for this segment. Pilot accepts the entity types, but its content and product gravity sit on VC-backed C-Corps. Indinero serves bootstrapped, PE-backed, LLC, S-Corp, and multi-entity growth companies, not just VC-backed Delaware C-Corps. Multi-entity structures or industries outside tech (construction, healthcare practice, nonprofit, professional services). Most-fit: Indinero, which publishes case studies across these verticals. Bookkeeper360 supports them but with less specialization. A clean migration checklist from Bench A 30/60/90-day migration from Bench, framed as the sequence any new provider should be willing to walk with you. None of this is exotic, it’s the discipline most ex-Bench customers wish their old provider had brought. Week 1: Recover and inventory. 1. Log into the Bench platform (now under Mainstreet) and export every available report, profit and loss statements, balance sheets, general ledger details, transaction registers, payroll exports if applicable. 2. Save copies of any tax returns Bench prepared. 3. Inventory which months are reconciled vs unreconciled. Note any open items. 4. Pull historical bank, credit card, and merchant processor statements directly from the source institutions for at least the prior 24 months as a backstop. Weeks 2 to 4: Provider selection and onboarding. 1. Shortlist providers against the cleavage lines in the prior section. 2. Run a fit conversation with two or three providers. Ask each: pricing transparency, GAAP posture, data portability, multi-state handling, R&D credit workflow, and how they handle catch-up work. 3. Make sure the new provider will own the migration, not just receive the export. Days 30 to 60: Catch-up and conversion. 1. The new provider rebuilds books inside QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite, avoid any provider that wants you on a proprietary platform. 2. If Bench was cash-basis and the new engagement is accrual, schedule the cash-to-accrual conversion explicitly. Per the AICPA’s audit and accounting guidance , this conversion requires recognition of accruals, deferrals, prepayments, and inventory adjustments at the conversion date. 3. Reconcile every account against the source-institution statements pulled in Week 1. 4. Identify any missed tax filings, federal, state income, state sales, and payroll. File extensions where necessary. Days 60 to 90: Forward-state hygiene. 1. Confirm the monthly close cadence with the new provider. A reasonable mid-market expectation is books closed within 10 to 15 business days of month-end. 2. Verify state nexus posture, especially for any state where you crossed the post- Wayfair economic-nexus threshold while on Bench. 3. If R&D-eligible, capture any prior-year credit you can claim via amended return. 4. Lock the new tax-prep workflow for the current tax year and confirm responsibility for federal and state filings. The faster you move through Week 1, the more options you keep. The Mainstreet portal export window will not stay open forever. When to choose Indinero over the others Indinero is the right answer for ex-Bench customers whose business has outgrown solo-bookkeeper economics but isn’t pure VC-backed Delaware C-Corp territory. Specifically, Indinero fits: Revenue in the $1M to $20M+ band, growing. This is the band where bookkeeping alone stops being enough and where in-house CFO economics still don’t pencil. The bundle replaces both. Any entity structure, C-Corp, S-Corp, LLC, or multi-entity. Any ownership model, bootstrapped, PE-backed, or VC-backed. None of those structures lock you out. Kruze and Burkland will turn you away if you’re outside the VC-funded Delaware C-Corp lane. Indinero won’t. Any industry, SaaS, ecommerce, construction, healthcare practice, nonprofit, or professional services. Indinero publishes case studies across all of them. You want bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and CFO advisory under one team rather than three vendor contracts. The fractional CFO services hub covers what that engagement actually looks like in practice. Pricing transparency matters. Indinero publishes its starting price ($750/mo, month-to-month) on its homepage. No annual prepay, no setup fees, no custom-quote runaround. Operational continuity matters. Indinero has been operating continuously since 2009 with stable ownership, a 5-star Clutch rating, and SOC 2 compliance (2026). After what Bench customers just lived through, “the same team will still be here in 24 months” is no longer a soft preference. The contrast with the other five providers stays factual. Pilot is the strong choice for early-stage VC-backed founders who want a clean app and don’t mind annual prepay. Kruze is the strong choice for funded Delaware C-Corps that want R&D-credit and 409A depth. Bookkeeper360 is the strong choice for SMBs that want a low-cost bookkeeping spine with optional advisory bolt-ons. Zeni is the strong choice for AI-forward tech startups. Burkland is the strong choice for VC-backed startups that need a dedicated fractional CFO above all else. Indinero is the strong choice for the growth-stage operator that wants all of those service lines as one engagement, with the operational stability to outlast the next provider shake-up. Migrating from Bench shouldn’t feel like an emergency. With the right partner, it’s a 90-day reset that leaves you with cleaner books, a real CPA team, and a finance function you don’t have to think about every week. Reach out for a free consultation. We’d love to learn about your business and find where we can help. Frequently asked questions , – Why did Bench shut down and what does it mean for existing customers? Bench abruptly ceased operations on December 27, 2024, then was acquired three days later by Employer.com and rebranded as Mainstreet in August 2025. Roughly 12,000 customers lost access to their books days before tax season. Bankruptcy filings later revealed $2.8 million in cash against $65.4 million in liabilities. Existing customers should export every available report from the Mainstreet portal now and plan a migration before year-end 2025 closings, since the same entity may not be there in six months. What is the best Bench accounting alternative for a growing SaaS company? For growing SaaS companies in the $1M-$20M revenue band, Indinero is the strongest Bench alternative thanks to its bundled finance team. Indinero packages bookkeeping, accounting, tax filing, and fractional CFO advisory under one fixed monthly engagement starting at $750/mo, month-to-month, no annual prepay. Pilot is the strong choice for early-stage VC-backed founders who want a clean web app. Kruze fits funded Delaware C-Corps needing R&D credit and 409A depth. How long does it take to migrate from Bench to a new bookkeeping provider? A clean migration from Bench to a new bookkeeping provider takes roughly 30 to 90 days when sequenced properly. Week 1 is recovery and inventory, export every available report from the Mainstreet portal and pull 24 months of bank, credit card, and merchant statements as a backstop. Weeks 2 to 4 cover provider selection and onboarding. Days 30 to 90 handle catch-up reconciliations, cash-to-accrual conversion if needed, multi-state nexus checks, and forward-state hygiene with a confirmed month-end close cadence. Will I lose my historical financial data if I leave Bench? You shouldn’t lose historical financial data if you export it from the Mainstreet portal promptly, but the export window won’t stay open forever. Bench used a proprietary bookkeeping platform, which is why Pilot publicly built a free Bench-to-QuickBooks migration service, the data isn’t natively portable. Save profit and loss statements, balance sheets, general ledgers, transaction registers, and any tax returns Bench prepared, then back everything up with statements pulled directly from your bank, credit card, and merchant processor for at least the prior 24 months. How does Indinero pricing compare to Bench’s old $299 per month plan? Indinero pricing starts at $750/mo, month-to-month, which is higher than Bench’s old $299/mo Essential tier but covers a broader scope. Bench’s $299/mo plan was cash-basis bookkeeping only. Tax-included tiers ran in the $600 to $700/mo band. Indinero’s entry engagement starts at $750/mo and scales into a bundled offering covering bookkeeping, GAAP-clean accrual accounting, tax filing, and fractional CFO advisory under one fixed monthly contract, with no annual prepay and no surprise upcharges. Can I get caught up on missed months of bookkeeping after Bench’s outages? Yes, a reputable replacement provider can rebuild missed months of bookkeeping after Bench’s outages, typically inside the first 30 to 60 days of the engagement. Catch-up work should be priced cleanly and separately, not buried inside an ambiguous onboarding fee. The new provider rebuilds your books inside QuickBooks Online, Xero, or NetSuite using statements pulled directly from your bank, credit card, and merchant processor. If Bench was cash-basis and you need accrual, schedule the cash-to-accrual conversion explicitly so accruals, deferrals, and prepayments are recognized at the conversion date. Do Bench alternatives handle tax filing as well as bookkeeping? Most Bench alternatives handle tax filing alongside bookkeeping, though the structure varies, some bundle it, others price it as a separate annual engagement. Indinero, Kruze, and Burkland embed tax inside the broader engagement. Pilot prices tax separately at $1,000 to $2,450+/year by entity. Bookkeeper360 runs roughly $1,000 to $1,500/year for business returns. Zeni’s tax tiers start at $2,499/year. For ex-Bench customers used to a combined bookkeeping-plus-tax bill, the bundled providers preserve that single-engagement model and keep partial-year filings, extensions, and R&D credit windows inside one team.

body_text: NIKE CAMPUS The Future of CX 2nd Annual Executive Gathering September 22 One Bowerman Drive Beaverton, Oregon An invitation-only, peer-led conversation for CX leaders reimagining care, navigating AI, and redefining differentiated service. During a moment of real disruption for customer care, CX executives are looking to their peers, not playbooks, for clarity. The Future of CX brings together senior leaders for candid conversations on what’s working, what’s not, and what’s next across customer experience and care. " * " indicates required fields What CX leaders are talking about today Session topics will include: How concepts like unreasonable hospitality are making their way into the strategies of customer care leaders Redefining live support and CX excellence in complex, high-stakes environments The evolving CX, product, and engineering operating model Where and why AI delivers measurable impact in customer care or falls short Executive-level lessons from recent AI deployments The day concludes with a private tour of the Nike campus, access to the Nike Employee Store, and an intimate networking dinner. Attendees can take advantage of preferred group rates, including breakfast, at either the AC Hotel Beaverton ($169/night, available through September 7) or the Hyatt House Portland/Beaverton ($147/night available through September 4). Please reserve your accommodations before the applicable cutoff dates to secure the discounted rate.

title: IDEX Health & Science Receives Silver Honoree Innovators Award for BrightLine 2.0
summary: Our Semrock BrightLine 2.0 filter set family has been distinguished among the best in the industry by the 2025 Laser Focus World Innovators’ Awards.
body_text: Rochester, New York, December 23, 2025 – IDEX Health & Science Honored by 2025 Laser Focus World Innovators Awards IDEX Health & Science, a leading innovator in optics and photonics, proudly announces that its cutting-edge Semrock BrightLine 2.0 filter set family has been distinguished among the best in the industry by the esteemed 2025 Laser Focus World Innovators’ Awards. title: Flowly Article Club: “Chronic Pain is a Hidden Epidemic. It’s Time for a Revolution” by Jennifer Kahn
body_text: With all the conversation going on about chronic pain, we wanted to expand on how we introduce our Flowly Article Club to keep you updated on the most recent updates and stories around pain management. This week, Flowly team member Christine wanted to share a recent article from the NY Times Magazine. ‍ What is the article about? “ Chronic Pain is a Hidden Epidemic. It’s Time for a Revolution ” discusses chronic pain, exploring its prevalence, the challenges in understanding and treating it, and the promising new research that offers hope for more effective therapies. The author, Jennifer Kahn, shares her personal experience with chronic arm pain. She describes the sudden onset of pain, the frustrating search for a diagnosis, and the limited effectiveness of existing treatment options. Chronic pain affects an estimated 100 million Americans and 2 billion people globally , making it more common than diabetes, heart disease, and cancer combined. Despite this, research on pain has been historically underfunded, leaving medical professionals with a limited understanding of its causes and mechanisms. Chronic pain can arise from a variety of factors, including injuries, surgeries, autoimmune diseases, and nerve damage. It is now recognized that chronic pain can be a disease itself, characterized by the sensitization of nerves in the body, leading to persistent pain signals. Historically, scientists struggled to understand why some individuals develop chronic pain while others with similar injuries do not. The discovery that pain-signaling pathways can become dysfunctional was a crucial breakthrough. The opioid epidemic brought renewed attention to the urgent need for effective pain management strategies. While opioids can provide temporary relief, they carry significant risks and side effects. The lack of alternative treatments has left many patients feeling desperate and abandoned by the medical system. Recent research initiatives, such as the HEAL initiative , are driving progress in understanding chronic pain and developing new treatment approaches. Scientists are beginning to uncover the complex biological mechanisms underlying chronic pain, paving the way for more targeted therapies. One promising area of research focuses on sodium-ion channels encoded by certain genes, specifically NaV 1.7, which play a crucial role in acting as the starting gate for pain signals. Other research avenues include developing targeted analgesics that specifically block pain receptors in nerves without affecting other organs and exploring treatments that address nerve degeneration in conditions like peripheral neuropathy. Beyond pharmacological interventions, there is a growing recognition of the importance of personalized treatment plans and ongoing support for chronic pain patients. Specialized pain clinics, such as the Center for Pain Medicine at UCSF, provide comprehensive care that addresses the multifaceted nature of chronic pain. These clinics offer a range of resources, including physical therapy, acupuncture, psychological support, and access to specialized pain management experts. Jennifer Kahn concludes by expressing cautious optimism about the future of chronic pain treatment. While a complete cure remains elusive, she highlights the significant strides being made in research and the growing awareness of the need for compassionate and comprehensive care for those living with chronic pain. How does it relate to Flowly and/or our community? Flowly is the subject of NIH-backed clinical trials, and we’re part of NIH’s HEAL initiative and are part of the larger movement trying to expand access and knowledge around pain management. Our approach to nonstructural pain is around giving our Heroes the tools they need to learn not only how to calm and regulate their nervous system but also the guidance and support they need from licensed pain therapists to reframe their thinking around pain. While this is a longer read, I think this article would bring some optimism to our Heroes - and those affected by chronic pain - in knowing that there is a massive paradigm shift when it comes to pain management, and we’re starting to see the healthcare industry embrace that pain requires a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach. Have an article you would like to share with the Flowly community? Send us an email at contact@flowly.world. The views expressed in this blog are solely those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect the opinions or position of Flowly. ‍

title: Photoroom vs VistaCreate: which tool wins for branded visuals?
summary: Photoroom vs VistaCreate compared: features, pricing, pros and cons. Find out which tool is best for creating fast, branded visuals at scale.
body_text: Choosing the right e‑commerce visual production tool can feel like finding a needle in a haystack. The options are endless, and every platform claims to be the solution. But one truth is universal—whether you’re running an e‑commerce shop, managing social media, or building a brand, you need polished visuals fast. So which tool should you choose? We can’t review all the platforms on the market, so this article is focused on one question: Photoroom vs VistaCreate: which tool is best for creating branded visuals quickly? Both platforms promise to simplify design for non-designers. But they’re built for very different needs. Photoroom is best for sellers that want to create e‑commerce visuals at scale, while VistaCreate is best for creators that need template-driven graphic design, social content, and presentations. Photoroom vs. VistaCreate at a glance If you’re short on time, here’s a quick comparison of Photoroom vs. VistaCreate. Feature Photoroom VistaCreate Background remover Best-in-class, instant, optimized for product photography Effective but less precise AI tools AI Backgrounds, Batch Editing, Virtual Model, Product Staging, AI Image Generation, AI Retouch AI Image Generator, Background and Object Remover Templates Branded, themed, and marketplace specific templates for sellers 200K+ templates for social and marketing Ease of use Mobile-first, minimal learning curve Drag-and-drop, template-driven Pricing Free plan available Pro: $12.99/month or $90/year Max: $34.99/month or $251,88/year Ultra: From $99/month or $990/year Free plan + Pro at $10/month Best for E‑commerce visuals, product photos, scaling fast Social content, presentations, team projects What is Photoroom? Photoroom is an AI-powered product photography platform built for e‑commerce sellers. Unlike general design platforms, its primary focus is turning raw product shots into polished, sales-ready images in seconds. Think of it as your product photography team for e‑commerce, without the high costs or steep learning curve. Photoroom works on iOS , Android , and desktop . Its interface is minimal, designed for speed and simplicity so you can go from photo to professional result in just a few clicks. Who is Photoroom for? E‑commerce sellers who need marketplace-ready product photos Small businesses and SMBs that want polished branding without a studio Marketers creating fast, consistent ad creatives at scale Makers and resellers who need professional photos to compete with larger brands Why choose Photoroom? The platform combines powerful AI tools with an easy-to-use interface built for sellers. Key features include: Best-in-class Background Remover for clean cutouts. Batch Mode to edit dozens of images at once. AI Backgrounds and AI Shadows for professional, branded scenes. Virtual Model and Product Staging for realistic apparel and product visuals. A built-in Brand Kit to keep every design consistent. With Photoroom, you don’t need big company budgets or years of design experience to achieve professional results. You just need your product, a smartphone, and the Photoroom app. Photoroom is the fastest way for sellers to create professional e‑commerce visuals at scale. What is VisaCreate? VistaCreate is a template-powered graphic design platform built for creators, marketers, and small teams that need professional visuals without starting from scratch. Originally launched as Crello, it was rebranded after joining the VistaPrint family in 2021 and now serves millions of users worldwide. Unlike Photoroom, which is optimized for product photography, VistaCreate takes a Canva-style approach. Its strength lies in providing a massive library of pre-made assets you can adapt for any channel—from social posts to flyers and presentations. Who is VistaCreate for? Social media creators who need posts, Stories, and Reels ready in minutes. Small businesses producing flyers, business cards, and digital ads. Marketing teams running multi-channel campaigns. Educators and event planners designing presentations, invitations, and printables. Why choose VistaCreate? The platform is built around templates and stock assets, with simple drag-and-drop editing. Key features include: 200K+ templates for nearly every design format. Millions of photos, videos, and vectors included in the Pro plan. Animations and video tools for motion graphics and social reels. A built-in Brand Kit to apply your colors and fonts consistently. Collaboration features for up to 10 team members in one Pro subscription. VistaCreate’s focus is versatility. It’s less about crafting product photos and more about giving you everything you need to build social content and marketing visuals fast. VistaCreate is the best solution for creators that want a large library of templates and stock assets. It’s not built for e‑commerce product photos like Photoroom. Feature comparison: Photoroom vs. VistaCreate Both Photoroom and VistaCreate help non-designers create professional visuals in minutes. But their strengths lie in fundamentally different areas, which make them suitable for different users and businesses. Here’s how they compare across the core features that matter most. Ease of use and workflow Photoroom is designed for speed . Its minimalist interface means you can go from raw photo to polished visual in a few clicks. It works seamlessly on mobile devices and desktop, letting you shoot on your phone and finish editing on desktop. Photoroom has no steep learning curve, and most users are up and running within minutes. Here’s how Photoroom speeds up your design workflow: Mobile-first design makes it ideal for sellers working on the go. Desktop application that lets you start work on one device, and finish on another. Batch Mode saves hours by processing multiple photos at once. Simple design workflows that avoid complex application menus or editing layers. VistaCreate, by contrast, feels more like a design studio. It’s template-rich and flexible, but that also means more choices to sift through and a potentially steeper learning curve. VistaCreate’s interface and workflows include: Drag-and-drop editor is intuitive but can feel heavier than Photoroom Heavier emphasis on desktop workflows as the the mobile app is less refined that Photoroom’s Collaboration tools that help teams work together, but add a layer of complexity to simple image creation and editing workflow Photoroom is the better platform for sellers to create and edit product photos, while VistaCreate offers more options for creators comfortable with templates. AI capabilities Photoroom takes an AI-first approach to photo editing, with tools purpose-built for e‑commerce workflows. From automatic background removal to generative AI tools to virtual models, Photoroom’s AI features save time while delivering professional results in seconds. Some of Photoroom’s AI tools include: Background Remover with best-in-class accuracy AI Backgrounds for branded, realistic scenes AI Shadows for studio-quality depth Virtual Model and Product Staging for lifelike visuals VistaCreate uses AI as a complement to its template engine. Its tools are useful, but they don’t match Photoroom’s precision for product photos. VistaCreate’s AI features include: Background Remover (Pro) AI Image Generator for new assets AI Object Remover for quick cleanups Sticker Maker for reusable design elements Photoroom’s AI capabilities are designed to create consistent, high-quality product visuals, while VistaCreate’s AI works for light editing but isn’t core to the platform. Customization and branding Photoroom focuses on helping businesses create consistent, brand-ready visuals that can be quickly created, exported, and uploaded across a variety of seller channels and marketplaces. Photoroom’s customization and branding features include: Brand Kit for logos, fonts, and colors Reusable templates for consistent ads and product shots Marketplace-optimized exports for Amazon, Shopify, Etsy VistaCreate also offers extensive branding and customization features that are ideal for teams and creators who want access to as many styles and templates as possible. VistaCreate’s customization and branding features include: Brand Kit (one brand on free plan, multiple on Pro) 200K+ templates adaptable to your brand palette Millions of stock photos, videos, and vectors Photoroom is best for businesses that need tight consistency across product visuals, while VistaCreate shines if you want flexibility across design formats. Output quality and speed Photoroom is built to deliver studio-quality product photos at scale. Its strength lies in fast automation that transforms raw product shots into professional, sales-ready visuals in minutes. Here’s how Photoroom ensures quality and speed: Batch Mode for product photo exports at scale AI-powered shadows and backgrounds for studio realism Optimized exports for e‑commerce marketplaces Export formats: JPG, PNG, high-res Instant sharing for listings or ads VistaCreate takes a different approach. It’s designed for polished layouts and creative versatility, making it ideal for marketing and campaign visuals. Its batch editing works across design canvases, helping teams update multiple branded templates at once. VistaCreate’s quality and speed features include: Batch editing across canvases (text, colors, synced layers) Professional templates for campaigns and print Export formats: JPG, PNG, PDF, GIF Instant sharing via link, embed, or direct publishing Photoroom is the better option for bulk photo editing that gets products marketplace-ready, while VistaCreate is better for creating design variations for marketing and sales campaigns. Pricing: Photoroom vs. VistaCreate Both Photoroom and VistaCreate offer free and paid tiers, but the way they structure their plans reflects their priorities: Photoroom around AI-powered product editing, VistaCreate around template access and collaboration. Plan Photoroom VistaCreate Free Up to 250 exports/month, limited AI tools Generous template + asset access, 1 Brand Kit Pro $7.50 per month/billed annually $12.99 per month /billed monthly Includes: Advanced AI tools (Product Staging, Virtual Model, Ghost Mannequin...) 5x AI image credit allowance 500 Batch exports per month 1000+ templates High resolution exports $10/month 200K+ templates, 170M assets, background remover, 10-user collaboration Max $20.99 per month/billed annually $34.99 per month/billed monthly Includes: Everything in the Pro plan Access to better AI models 3x Pro AI image/video credit allowance 1,500 Batch exports per month Faster processing times Priority customer support N/A Ultra From $82.50 per month/billed annually From $99 per month/billed monthly Includes: Everything in the Max plan Access to our best AI models AI credits increase with each Ultra tier Fastest processing times Advanced AI workflows Enterprise Contact the sales team for pricing N/A You can find more information about what each Photoroom's plan includes on the dedicated pricing page . Photoroom’s pricing scales with volume and AI power, making it ideal for businesses that depend on product visuals. VistaCreate offers excellent value for small teams that need broad design assets and collaboration at a low monthly cost. Photoroom vs. VistaCreate: Pros and cons of each tool Every e‑commerce visual production tool has its strengths and limitations. Here’s a list of pros and cons for Photoroom and VistaCreate. Photoroom: Pros and cons Pros Cons Best-in-class Background Remover built for e‑commerce product photos AI-first toolkit, including Batch Mode, Virtual Model, Instant Shadows, Product Staging Mobile-first workflows with seamless desktop access Marketplace-ready exports sized for Amazon, Shopify, Etsy Proven business impact: users report faster workflows and higher conversions Smaller template library compared to VistaCreate Free plan is capped at 250 exports/month Less suited for multi-page creative projects like presentations Photoroom is the best option for sellers that want to create e‑commerce visuals at scale. VistaCreate: Pros and cons Pros Cons 200K+ templates covering social, print, and campaign formats Rich stock library with millions of photos, videos, and vectors Video and animation tools for dynamic content Collaboration for up to 10 users on Pro Batch editing for text, colors, and synced design elements AI tools are less precise than Photoroom’s Heavier learning curve with more menus and options Mobile app experience lags behind desktop Occasional reports of lag or export glitches VistaCreate is best for creators and teams that need a large template library and stock assets to scale design output. Which tool should you choose? Both Photoroom and VistaCreate are strong e‑commerce visual production tools. But the right choice depends on what you need to create. Here’s how the two platforms stack up across common use cases: E‑commerce → Photoroom. Create product photos that are marketplace-ready in minutes with AI-powered background removal, shadows, and batch exports. Social content → VistaCreate. Access 200K+ templates, animations, and stock assets to design posts, Stories, and Reels fast. Marketing campaigns and branded visuals → Photoroom. Use the Brand Kit, reusable templates, and AI Backgrounds to keep campaigns consistent and polished across every channel. Presentation-style design → VistaCreate. Build professional decks, flyers, and invitations with drag-and-drop layouts and easy brand styling. Scaling visuals fast → Photoroom. Batch Mode and automation let you process large catalogs or campaigns at speed, saving hours of editing. Photoroom is the best tool for sellers looking to create and scale professional product visuals, while VisaCreate is a tool more suited to creators and teams that want extensive template libraries and stock design assets. Final verdict VistaCreate is versatile for social posts, presentations, and creative campaigns. Photoroom is the must-have tool for e‑commerce sellers and small businesses that need fast, scalable product visuals. Many teams may use both tools side by side, but if you have to choose one, and your priority is scaling branded content and driving sales, Photoroom delivers the speed and reliability competitors can’t match.

title: Best online English classes for kids: what to look for and where to start
summary: The best online English classes for kids depend on the goal: writing, grammar, reading, or ESL. Here's what to look for, how the main options compare, what they cost, and how to match a class to your kid.
body_text: "English" is the subject parents most often mean two completely different things by. For one family it's grammar and writing mechanics. For another it's reading comprehension and literature. For a third it's English as a second language. The best online English class for your kid depends entirely on which of those you're actually trying to solve, and the good news is that a live, small-group class can target any of them far better than a one-size-fits-all workbook. This guide breaks down what "English" really covers, what to look for in a class, how the main options compare, and how to match one to your kid. What "English" actually means when you're shopping for a class Before you enroll, get specific about the goal. English classes for kids usually fall into one of these buckets: Writing and composition: essays, creative writing, paragraph structure, editing. If your kid can talk your ear off but freezes at a blank page, this is the bucket. Grammar and mechanics: parts of speech, punctuation, sentence structure. Useful as a targeted fix, less useful as a standalone year-long class. Reading and literature: comprehension, analysis, book discussion. Great for kids who read the words but miss the meaning, or strong readers who are ready to dig deeper. English language learning (ESL): for kids building English as an additional language, where a patient live teacher matters enormously. Naming the bucket first saves you from the vague "language arts" class that tries to do everything and goes deep on nothing. What makes an online English class worth it? Live feedback on real work. Writing improves through revision and specific feedback, which is one of the most consistent findings in the research on effective writing instruction. [1] A recorded video can't read your kid's paragraph and tell them why the second sentence is confusing. A live teacher can. Small groups and discussion. English is a discussion subject. Reading analysis and writing both get better when kids hear other kids' takes and defend their own. Smaller classes give every kid airtime and let the teacher tailor to each one. [2] A narrow, honest focus. A class called "5-week persuasive essay workshop" will almost always beat "English for 4th graders," because the teacher knows exactly what they're building toward. Subject-matter expertise. Look at who's teaching. A literature discussion led by someone who genuinely loves books, or a grammar class from a teacher who makes mechanics click, is a different experience than a generalist working from a script. The main online English options, compared honestly No single option wins for everyone. Here's the real landscape: Outschool is a marketplace of live, small-group and 1:1 English classes taught by independent teachers, from single-session writing workshops to multi-week literature or grammar courses, plus book clubs and ESL. Strength: you can match a specific format and teacher to the exact bucket your kid needs, with live feedback. Trade-off: because it's a marketplace, quality varies by teacher, so read reviews and check backgrounds. IEW (Institute for Excellence in Writing) is a well-loved homeschool writing curriculum you teach yourself or follow through recorded video (Andrew Pudewa's "Structure and Style for Students"). Strength: a rigorous, proven method that gives writing a clear structure. Trade-off: you're the teacher, or your kid is learning from a screen with no one reading their actual writing and responding to it. If you'd rather have a live teacher run the IEW method with your kid, that's exactly what a marketplace fills, you'll find live IEW classes on Outschool taught by teachers trained in it. Khan Academy offers free grammar and reading lessons for a range of ages. Strength: cost and structure. Trade-off: self-paced and independent, with no live discussion or writing feedback. Local tutoring or a writing center gives you in-person attention. Strength: face-to-face rapport. Trade-off: cost, scheduling, and a much smaller pool of specialists than you can reach online. The pattern: for a curriculum you deliver yourself or self-paced practice, IEW and free tools are fine. For writing feedback and real discussion, you want a live teacher, which is what a marketplace like online English classes on Outschool is built for.
